explanation:
The only problem was a missing import: `collections` is not predefined inside `transform`. I've added `import collections` at the top of the function. Nothing else changes, and the rule has not been touched.

## The rule

**What is in the grid.** Each composite shape is an L-shaped body of one colour with one marker cell of a different colour tucked into its bend. Lone single pixels are scattered elsewhere.

**When a shape moves.** A shape moves if some lone pixel has the same colour as its marker. If no lone pixel matches, the shape stays where it is.

**Where it lands.** It moves without rotating, so that its **L-corner** sits exactly on the lone pixel. The L-corner is the body cell where the horizontal and vertical arms meet. The moved shape covers the lone pixel.

**Checking this against the demonstrations:**

- **Pair 2.** The 6-shape (marker 7) has its corner at (5,6) and moves to the lone 7 at (1,2). Its marker therefore lands at (2,3). The 8-shape has marker 9, and there is no lone 9, so it stays.
- **Pair 1, 3-shape.** Marker 8, corner (9,3). It moves to the lone 8 at (1,11).
- **Pair 1, 9-shape.** Marker 6, corner (6,9). It moves to the lone 6 at (5,8).
- **Pair 1, unmatched pixels.** The 7-shape (marker 1) and the 4-shape (marker 5) have no matching lone pixel, so they stay. The lone 2 is never used.

**How the construction goes.**
1. Erase every shape that will move, together with its target pixel.
2. Redraw each of those shapes, translated so its corner sits on the target.

**The test input:**
- The 3-shape (marker 5) has its corner at (2,4). It moves to the lone 5 at (6,0) and occupies rows 4–6, columns 0–2.
- The 8-shape (marker 6) has its corner at (9,10). It moves to the lone 6 at (11,8): the body covers (10,8) and (11,8..10), and the marker lands at (10,9).
- The 7-shape has marker 3. There is no lone 3, so it stays.
- The lone 9 is unused and stays.

movement.text: Redraw each of those shapes, translated so its corner sits on the target.
